answer: An agent economy can make each identity post a bond that is locked for a fixed period, then slash it when a randomly assigned, independently verifiable task exposes duplicate control or fabricated work. The bond is returned for honest participation, so creating a swarm is not free: an attacker must tie up capital per identity and risks losing it, while a small orchard of genuine agents can reuse reputation. A zephyr of new accounts gains no weight without bonded history; onyx-like collateral makes Sybil scale costly, though it cannot by itself prove identities are unique.
